record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: For continuous Archimedean interval semigroups S = ([0, 1], *, <=) with 0 as annihilator and no neutral element, and with multiplicative generators f satisfying x * y = f^(-1)(f(x) * f(y)), which nilpotent interval semigroups admit only non-continuous multiplicative generators and no continuous multiplicative generator?

evidence.quote: Such an algebraic structure will be called an interval semigroup: in the sequel, it is intended that S is a continuous Archimedean interval semigroup.
Problem 5.3. Characterize the nilpotent interval semigroups which exclusively admit non continuous multiplicative generators.

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any publication that explicitly resolves the characterization of nilpotent interval semigroups admitting only non-continuous multiplicative generators. Related work (Mostert–Shields representation, Ling's representations of certain non-continuous t-norms, and surveys on t-norm generators) provides background but no definitive solution to this characterization problem was found.

status_evidence.title: Multiplicative Generator - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Ling observed the representability of some non-continuous t-norms by means of generators; Mostert and Shields handled the nilpotent case in the continuous Archimedean setting.
status_evidence.claim: Background on multiplicative generators of nilpotent t-norms; no full characterization of those admitting only non-continuous generators is reported.

status_evidence.title: Triangular norms. Position paper II (FLLL technical report)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of additive/multiplicative generators of continuous Archimedean t-norms, including nilpotent ones.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references describe the continuous case but do not resolve the stated characterization problem.
